title: Avoidance before accumulated simulation cost
statement: Let $M$ and $N$ be multi-tape Turing machines, let $e$ map configurations of $M$ to configurations of $N$, let $q$ assign a natural-number simulation cost to each configuration of $M$, and let $X$ and $X'$ be sets of states (including the possible halting state) of $M$ and $N$, respectively. Assume that for every configuration $c$ whose state is outside $X$, running $N$ from $e(c)$ for $q(c)$ steps yields the encoding of the next configuration of $M$; that if $c$ has state in $X$, then $e(c)$ has state in $X'$; and that, for every such $c$, the run of $N$ from $e(c)$ has state outside $X'$ at every time strictly less than $q(c)$. If the run of $M$ from an initial configuration $d$ has state outside $X$ at every time $u<t$, then the run of $N$ from $e(d)$ has state outside $X'$ at every time strictly less than $\sum_{u=0}^{t-1} q(M^u(d))$, where $M^u(d)$ denotes the configuration reached after $u$ steps.
